patients.summary: Healthy field sales representative who joined in 2024. A 2025 bicycle crash caused a traumatic pancreatic injury managed without surgery; a car crash that November caused intra-abdominal bleeding needing laparotomy; a third crash in July 2026, after his last visit, put him in a trauma ICU in hemorrhagic shock, known to the practice only from the faxed admission note.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is 27, looking for a primary care doctor closer to home; his old office is an hour-plus drive and hard to reach. No current issues, no meds. Wants a physical and to get set up. Booked new patient physical 6/11 at 8:30 (he asked for early, he's on the road most days). Insurance card photo received through the portal. Records release form emailed to him for his prior primary care office.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27M joining the practice. Sales rep, covers a big territory and spends a lot of the day in the car. Feels well, nothing he wants addressed today, mostly wants a doctor he can reach.

PMH: none. Never hospitalized. No surgeries.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: dad has hypertension, well controlled on treatment. Mom has an underactive thyroid. He knows of no bleeding problems or blood disorders on either side.
Social: single, rents in Northampton. Never smoked, no vaping. A drink or two a month at most. Runs and bikes on weekends when he can.

ROS negative across the board.

Exam: pleasant, fit-appearing. Vitals as recorded, BMI about 24. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses or organomegaly. Skin without concerning moles. Neuro grossly intact. Mood bright.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 1.

A/P: healthy adult male, preventive visit.
- Can't recall his last tetanus shot, probably high school. Tdap today.
- One-time HIV and hep C screens, baseline lipids, CBC, CMP drawn.
- Seatbelt and bike helmet counseling given, he says he always wears both.
- Release signed for his former primary care office.
- Flu and COVID this fall at a nurse visit.
- Back in a year for his physical, call or text sooner if anything.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Jacob, all of your blood work came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver numbers, sugar and cholesterol all in the normal range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do here. Good to meet you on Tuesday.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Great, thanks for getting back to me so fast.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Prior primary care records received by fax, 14 pages, covering roughly 2016 to 2022. Annual physicals with normal exams, a sports physical form, routine CBC and metabolic panels within normal limits. No diagnoses on their problem list, no prescriptions on file, no drug allergies listed. No vaccine dates beyond childhood series attached. Filed to media for the PCP.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In before his first call of the day. Feeling well, no fever. No prior vaccine reactions. Flu shot left deltoid, 2024-25 COVID booster right deltoid. Waited 15 min, no issues. VIS sheets given.

events.reason: upper abdominal pain and nausea after bicycle crash

reports.text: Indication: epigastric pain and nausea five days after blunt injury to the upper abdomen. Technique: real-time grayscale and color imaging of the abdomen. Findings: Liver normal in size and echotexture without focal lesion. Gallbladder without stones or wall thickening; common duct not dilated. Pancreas partly obscured by bowel gas; a small fluid collection is seen alongside the pancreas. Spleen and both kidneys normal in size, no hydronephrosis. Abdominal aorta normal caliber. No free fluid in the hepatorenal or splenorenal spaces or the pelvis.
reports.conclusion: Small peripancreatic fluid collection. Otherwise unremarkable abdominal ultrasound.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Emergency Department Provider Note (regional hospital)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 03/22/2025

CC: belly pain and queasiness x 2 days.

HPI: 28 y/o male (DOB 6/29/1996) who went over the handlebars of his bike on 3/17 after a car pulled into him. He came down with the upper belly on the edge of a curb. People at the scene looked him over, he felt okay and went home without being seen. Since Thursday he has had steady upper abdominal aching and nausea that are not getting better, prompting today's visit. No vomiting of blood, no black stools, no fever.

PMH none. Meds none. Allergies: NKDA. FHx: father HTN, mother hypothyroid, no bleeding disorders in the family. SHx: never smoker, rare alcohol, outside sales.

VS within normal limits (see flowsheet).
Exam: uncomfortable but nontoxic. Abdomen soft, tender in the epigastrium, no rebound, no guarding. No bruising over the abdomen. Lungs clear, heart regular.

Labs: Hgb 13.8, WBC 9.0. Amylase 450 (ref 30-110), lipase 210 (ref 0-160). LFTs normal.
US abdomen: small fluid collection next to the pancreas.

MDM: delayed presentation after a handlebar-type blow to the upper abdomen with elevated pancreatic enzymes and peripancreatic fluid. Consistent with traumatic injury to the pancreas. Hemodynamically normal, no peritoneal signs. Discussed with general surgery, who will admit for nonoperative management.

Dispo: admitted to surgery.

documents.title: Discharge Summary (regional hospital)
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — GENERAL SURGERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 03/22/2025, discharged 03/25/2025.

Diagnoses: traumatic pancreatic injury; blunt abdominal trauma (bicycle crash 03/17/2025).

Course: admitted from the ED for nonoperative care. Kept NPO with IV fluids the first day, serial abdominal exams remained benign, pain improved. Clear liquids started hospital day 2 and advanced to a regular low-fat diet, which he tolerated. Ambulating, pain controlled with acetaminophen. Stable for discharge home.

Discharge meds: acetaminophen over the counter as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Instructions: low-fat diet for two weeks, no contact sports or cycling until cleared, return for worsening pain, vomiting or fever. Follow up with PCP in 1 week.

Records sent on request of the patient's primary care office.

documents.title: Was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just wanted to let you know I was in the hospital since Saturday. I had a bike crash last week and my stomach kept hurting so I went to the ER. They said I bruised my pancreas and kept me a few days. I got out yesterday. They told me to see my doctor in a week. Do you want to see me?

documents.title: RE: Was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry to hear it, glad you're home. Yes, I'd like to see you. The front desk will set you up early next week. We'll ask the hospital for the records. In the meantime keep the diet light, and if the pain gets worse, you vomit or run a fever, go back in.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request to regional hospital medical records for ED note, discharge summary, labs and imaging 3/22-3/25. Pt scheduled 3/31 9:00.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after a 3-night stay at the regional hospital. Hospital records requested, not here yet; history is his.

Bike vs car 3/17, went over the bars and hit his upper belly on a curb. Felt okay at first. Two days later started aching in the upper abdomen with nausea, went to the ER on 3/22. Told his pancreas enzymes were up and there was fluid near the pancreas on ultrasound. Admitted, no surgery, nothing by mouth then diet advanced, home 3/25.

Today: aching is much better, 2/10, only after bigger meals. Nausea gone. Eating a low-fat diet. Normal BMs, no blood. No fever. Taking acetaminophen once a day or less. Bike is in the shop and he's not riding.

Exam: comfortable. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness high in the epigastrium, no guarding, no mass, normal bowel sounds. No bruising.

A/P: traumatic pancreatic injury, managed without surgery, recovering.
- Lipase and CBC today.
- Stay on a lighter diet another week or two, acetaminophen as needed, skip ibuprofen for now.
- No cycling until the soreness is fully gone.
- Call if pain returns or worsens, fevers, vomiting.
- Will review the hospital records when they come.

documents.title: Lipase result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lipase 52, back to normal. Blood count normal. Sent him a note.

documents.title: Labs from Monday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your pancreas enzyme is back in the normal range and your blood count looks good. Keep doing what you're doing. If the pain hasn't fully settled in a few weeks, let me know.

documents.title: Hospital records received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Regional hospital records for 3/22-3/25 finally received after a second fax request. ED note, discharge summary, labs and ultrasound report attached to the admission. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Cancel physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt left voicemail cancelling Friday's annual physical, has to cover an account two states over this week. Says he'll call back to reschedule once he has his travel calendar.

documents.title: Influenza vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: End-of-day slot. Well today. Flu vaccine given L deltoid, tolerated. Declined COVID booster this year, wants to wait. Reminded him he still owes us a physical; he'll book after the holidays.

events.reason: high-speed motor vehicle collision, abdominal pain

reports.text: Focused assessment with sonography for trauma, performed at the bedside. Hepatorenal recess: free fluid present. Splenorenal recess: no free fluid. Pelvis: no free fluid. Pericardial view: no effusion.
reports.conclusion: Positive FAST: free fluid in the hepatorenal recess. No other abnormality.

documents.title: Trauma Surgery Discharge Summary (regional hospital)
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL TRAUMA SERVICE — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission 11/07/2025, discharge 11/12/2025.
Patient: 29-year-old man.

Principal diagnosis: intra-abdominal hemorrhage requiring operative management, after blunt abdominal trauma.
Other: traumatic pancreatic injury earlier this year (managed nonoperatively, March 2025).
Allergies: NKDA. Home meds: none.

Presentation: restrained driver in a high-speed collision, airbags deployed. Arrived alert and anxious with diffuse abdominal pain. BP 110/70, HR 105, RR 22, SpO2 97% RA. Abdomen distended and tender in all four quadrants with a seatbelt mark across the lower abdomen; no rebound or guarding. FAST positive for free fluid in the hepatorenal recess, otherwise negative.

Course: taken emergently to the OR for exploratory laparotomy; hemoperitoneum evacuated and bleeding controlled. Recovered on the surgical floor, diet advanced, pain transitioned to oral agents, ambulating independently. Midline incision closed with staples, clean and dry at discharge.

Discharge meds: oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed for severe pain (#20, no refills); acetaminophen 1000 mg every 8 hours as needed.
Activity: no lifting over 15 lb, no driving while taking oxycodone.
Follow-up: trauma surgery clinic in 1-2 weeks for staple removal; PCP within 1 week.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours as needed for severe pain

documents.title: Pharmacy call, new opioid fill
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pharmacist called to confirm we are his PCP: filling oxycodone 5 mg #20 written by the regional hospital surgery team today. Nothing in our chart about a hospital stay.

Called pt. He was in a bad car accident last Friday, needed belly surgery for internal bleeding, discharged this morning. Pain okay, tolerating food, has not been driving. Hospital follow-up booked 11/18 with PCP. Discharge summary requested from the hospital. PCP aware.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets by mouth every 8 hours as needed for pain

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
29M seen 6 days after discharge. Discharge summary from the regional hospital arrived 11/14 and reviewed; no operative report came with it.

Restrained driver, high-speed crash 11/7, airbags went off. Positive FAST, taken for exploratory laparotomy for intra-abdominal bleeding, bleeding controlled. Home 11/12. Second abdominal injury this year: pancreatic injury after the March bike crash, managed without surgery.

Now: incision sore, 3/10, worse getting out of bed. Using oxycodone about twice a day, mostly at night, plus acetaminophen. Eating small meals, BMs back, passing gas. No fever, no wound drainage, no vomiting. Not driving. Lightheaded once on standing the first day home, none since. Down about 4 kg since spring.

Meds: oxycodone 5 mg q6h prn (hospital), acetaminophen 1 g q8h prn. NKDA.

Exam: walking slowly but on his own. Vitals as charted. Midline abdominal incision with staples, edges together, no redness, no drainage. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender around the wound, not distended, bowel sounds present. Calves soft.

A/P:
1. S/p exploratory laparotomy for intra-abdominal hemorrhage after blunt abdominal trauma. Healing as expected. CBC today. Staples out at trauma clinic Friday.
2. Postop pain. Taper oxycodone over the next week, acetaminophen first. No driving on it.
3. Traumatic pancreatic injury, March, recovered.
4. Work note given: off work through 12/5, then reassess.
RTC 4 weeks.

documents.title: CBC result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 11.9 a week and a half after surgery for bleeding, as expected. Recheck at his next visit. Messaged pt.

documents.title: Trauma Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL TRAUMA SURGERY CLINIC
Visit date: 11/21/2025
Re: Jacob Murphy, DOB 06/29/1996

Thank you for allowing us to share in his care. He returns two weeks after exploratory laparotomy for hemoperitoneum following a motor vehicle collision. Recovering well at home, appetite returning, pain improving.

Allergies: NKDA. Meds: oxycodone as needed (tapering), acetaminophen.

Exam: afebrile. Midline wound healed without erythema or drainage. Staples removed. Abdomen soft, nondistended.

Plan: no lifting over 15 pounds for six weeks from surgery, then advance activity as tolerated. Return to us as needed; no routine follow-up planned.

Trauma Surgery

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six weeks out from laparotomy. Staples came out at the trauma clinic 11/21 per patient; their letter has not reached us.

Feels close to normal. Finished the oxycodone the week after our last visit, uses acetaminophen rarely. Eating normally, weight coming back. Back at work since 12/8 doing phone and local accounts, not lifting sample cases yet. Driving again, a little tense in traffic at first, better now. Sleeping fine. No nightmares or flashbacks about the crash.

PHQ-9 3, GAD-7 4.

Exam: well. Midline scar healed, no hernia with cough, nontender.

A/P: recovered from exploratory laparotomy for traumatic intra-abdominal bleeding. Hgb rechecked today. Light duty until the six-week lifting limit is up in early January, then advance as tolerated. Off opioids. Resolving the acute injury problems on his list. Physical in the spring.

documents.title: CBC result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 13.4, recovering. Messaged him, no further checks needed before his physical.

documents.title: Trauma clinic letter received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Trauma surgery clinic letter for the 11/21/2025 visit came in by fax today, seven weeks after the visit. Attached to that visit and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Back to full duty?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Morning. My manager wants me back on the road full time with the display cases starting next week. The surgeon said no lifting for six weeks and it's been more than that. Am I good to go? HR wants something in writing.

documents.title: RE: Back to full duty?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, the surgeon's six-week limit is over and your exam last month was fine. Ease into the heavier lifting over a couple of weeks. A return-to-work letter, no restrictions, is in your documents tab now.

documents.title: Scheduling
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to book the physical he skipped last year. Fri 4/17 8:00, fasting labs same morning.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
29M for his physical, first since his new-patient visit. A rough 2025: bike crash in March with a pancreatic injury handled without surgery, then the car crash in November with intra-abdominal bleeding and an exploratory laparotomy.

Feels well. Full duty at work since January, lifting the display cases without trouble. Appetite normal, weight nearly back. No belly pain, no change in bowels, no greasy stools. Has not gotten back on the bike yet, may this summer. Always wears his seatbelt. Sleep okay, mood good.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father HTN, mother hypothyroid, no bleeding disorders. Unchanged.
Social: never smoker, a drink or two a month.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 1.

Exam: well. Vitals as recorded. HEENT normal. Neck without thyroid enlargement. Heart regular without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen: healed midline laparotomy scar, no hernia standing or with cough, soft, nontender, no masses. Skin otherwise unremarkable. Extremities without edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P:
1. Preventive care, healthy 29 y/o man. CBC, CMP, lipids this morning. Tdap 2024. Flu shot each fall; COVID when he wants it.
2. History of traumatic pancreatic injury and of laparotomy for traumatic intra-abdominal bleeding, recovered. Nothing further needed now.
3. Counseled on helmet when he does ride again.
Next physical in a year.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Jacob, your labs from Friday all look good. Your blood count is fully back to normal at 14.4, and your kidney, liver, sugar and cholesterol numbers are all in range. See you next spring.

documents.title: RE: Physical labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Awesome, thank you!

reports.text: Bedside focused assessment with sonography for trauma. Hepatorenal recess: free fluid. Splenorenal recess: free fluid. Pelvis and pericardial views without additional abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Positive FAST, free fluid in the hepatorenal and splenorenal recesses.

documents.title: Trauma ICU Admission Note (regional hospital)
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — SURGICAL ICU / TRAUMA SERVICE
Date of service: 07/16/2026
Reason: high-speed motor vehicle collision with signs of hemorrhagic shock.

HPI: 30-year-old man, restrained driver in a high-speed collision, airbag deployment. On arrival he is awake and anxious, sweating. Prior history: traumatic pancreatic injury (March 2025) and intra-abdominal hemorrhage that required laparotomy (November 2025).

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA. FHx: father with treated hypertension, mother with hypothyroidism, no bleeding or blood disorders. SHx: never smoker, alcohol 1-2 drinks a month, field sales.

Vitals: BP 90/60, HR 120, RR 22, SpO2 97% on room air.
Exam: abdomen distended with guarding and diffuse tenderness. Healed midline incision. Secondary survey finds no other injury.
FAST: free fluid in the hepatorenal and splenorenal recesses.

Assessment: hemorrhagic shock from intra-abdominal bleeding after blunt abdominal trauma, in a patient with a prior laparotomy.
Plan: resuscitation and operative exploration; ICU care to follow.

[Faxed to primary care office 07/24/2026. No further pages.]

documents.title: Hospital fax received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: One-document fax from the regional hospital trauma service: ICU admission note dated 7/16/2026. No discharge summary or operative note included. Attached to the admission and routed to PCP inbox.
